Well-preserved fourth-century quarters reveal details of daily life, urban development and economic activities

Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a well-preserved Byzantine-era city in the western desert.

The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

A leading higher education programme, aimed at keeping 1 million girls in school across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, has been axed by the British government just two years after it was announced.

guardian.description:
Indian prime minister has a habit of collecting awards on his travels, some as their first and only recipient

As Narendra Modi touched down in Seychelles over the weekend, the archipelago nation in the Indian Ocean swiftly bestowed one of its “highest” honours upon the Indian prime minister.

Modi beamed as he accepted the Guardian of the Blue Horizon award from Patrick Herminie, the Seychelles president, complete with a trophy and certificate.

guardian.description:
Authorities say rainy season getting deadlier, with Ghana reporting 13 dead and floods hitting Benin, Togo and Nigeria

Floods in Côte d’Ivoire have killed 59 people since May, the communication minister told a cabinet meeting in Abidjan.

There are fears the toll could further rise as rescue teams continue to search for victims during the rainy season, which runs from May until July, the minister, Amadou Coulibaly, added.

guardian.description:
Interim president says unrest will not break out despite anger at official response to the 24 June disaster

Venezuela’s interim president has defended her country’s emergency response to the twin earthquakes that have killed more than 3,000 people, vowing the country would not descend into social unrest.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger at what they see as the US-backed government’s inadequate response to the 24 June disaster before international teams arrived.

guardian.description:
Official statement offers the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual and fatal incident in Beijing

Chinese authorities said the man who flew a small plane into Beijing’s tallest skyscraper last week was a 66-year-old who had mental health problems.

The statement published on Thursday offered the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual incident that occurred in Beijing’s central business district on the evening of 26 June.

An 11-year-old boy has driven his parents’ truck into a Buddhist procession in Thailand, killing at least nine monks.

CCTV footage shared by a local rescue group showed the moment the monks, wearing orange robes, were run over as they walked in procession along a road. The timestamp on the footage was shortly before 11am local time on Thursday.

Many have called for the Reuters photo to receive the Pulitzer Prize.

euronews.title: OPEC+ agrees another modest output rise as oil prices fall back to pre-war levels
euronews.description: Seven countries in the OPEC+ alliance agreed to lift their combined oil output by a modest 188,000 barrels per day in August, adding supply just as crude prices slide back to levels not seen since before the Iran war erupted.

euronews.description: This Tuesday, NATO leaders land in Ankara for an annual summit. The pre-negotiated statement promises an iron-clad 32-member family committed to collective protection. However, the official documents are not always reflecting the reality.

rfi.title: Major wildfires burn in Southern France as early fire season hits Europe
rfi.description: Firefighters are fighting wildfires across southern France and other parts of Europe, and authorities are warning that this year’s fire season has started a month earlier than usual after early heatwaves in May and June left vegetation particularly dry and vulnerable.

rfi.title: Macron to become first Western European leader to visit post-Assad Syria
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron ​will visit ‌Syria to discuss ways to ​strengthen bilateral ​relations and issues of ⁠mutual interest, ​the Syrian presidency has announced, in what would be the first visit by a Western European head of state since Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

rfi.title: Tour de France bans spectators from third stage as fire burns in French Pyrenees
rfi.description: Spectators have been banned from the third stage of the Tour de France cycling race through the Pyrenees Monday, which will be adapted as a forest fire burns the area.

rfi.title: England survive Azteca thriller to set up last eight showdown with Norway
rfi.description: England moved into a last eight clash with Norway after they beat Mexico 3-2 in a whirlwind game for the ages at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

rfi.title: Haaland's late strikes take Norway past Brazil to last eight for first time
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice in the last 11 minutes to sweep Norway past Brazil into the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

rfi.title: Summit host Turkey eyes major weapons deals with NATO allies
rfi.description: Next week's NATO Summit in Ankara is expected to showcase Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s rising influence within the alliance, as he aims to use the gathering to overcome resistance to crucial arms deals and highlight the rapid growth of Turkey’s defence industry.

rfi.title: Three sons of Iran's slain leader Khamenei appear at funeral, not successor Mojtaba
rfi.description: Three sons of slain Iranian leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei prayed beside his coffin and those of four other family members on Sunday, but Mojtaba, the son who has succeeded him as Iran's supreme leader, ​did not make ‌an appearance.

rfi.title: World Cup bosses wipe out red card for US striker Balogun on eve of Belgium tie
rfi.description: World Cup organisers Fifa on Sunday rescinded the red card handed to the United States striker Folarin Balogun during his side's 2-0 victory in the last 32 over Bosnia and Herzegovina on 1 July.

rfi.title: France's richest man Bernard Arnault ordered to pay €22.5m in back taxes
rfi.description: Bernard Arnault, head of the luxury goods group LVMH, has been ordered to pay nearly €22.5 million in back taxes after a Paris appeals court overturned earlier rulings in his favour in a long-running dispute with the tax authorities.

rfi.title: From memes to political movement, India's 'Cockroach' party leads youth revolt
rfi.description: India's Cockroach Janata Party began life as a series of internet memes and has grown into a real-life movement, bringing together young people angry about unemployment and alleged exam fraud. What began five weeks ago as a satirical response to comments by India's chief justice has become a fast-growing campaign which now has political ambitions, even as observers question whether it can survive without more effective organisation.

rfi.title: The Afghan women farmers keeping their village alive
rfi.description: In a remote province of northeastern Afghanistan, women farmers are playing a vital role in their community's survival among the snow-capped mountains.

rfi.title: Hunger in northern Nigeria reaches worst levels in nearly a decade, WFP says
rfi.description: More than 17 million people across nine conflict-hit states in northern Nigeria face severe hunger, the UN's food agency (WFP) has said, warning that violence and funding ‌cuts are driving food insecurity to its worst level in nearly a decade. Stripped of their livelihoods, some people are fleeing across the border into neighbouring Benin.

rfi.title: Mbappé strikes to send France into last eight showdown with Morocco at World Cup
rfi.description: After a 1-0 win in Saturday's match against Paraguay, France will take on Morocco for the second consecutive World Cup. In 2022 in Qatar, they met to contest a place in the final. Four years later in the United States, they will play for a place in the semi-finals.

rfi.title: ‘International law is our compass’ in global conflict, UN rights chief tells RFI
rfi.description: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk tells RFI that repression in Iran and drone warfare and sexual violence in Sudan show that civilians are paying the highest price for conflicts around the globe.

rfi.title: Denmark's Vingegaard takes Tour de France lead with 'perfect start'
rfi.description: Jonas Vingegaard took the first leader's yellow jersey of the 113th edition of the Tour de France as his Visma-Lease a Bike outfit won Saturday's opening team time-trial in Barcelona.

rfi.title: Ounahi stars as Morocco outclass Canada to advance to last eight at World Cup
rfi.description: Azzedine Ounahi scored twice on Saturday to steer Morocco past Canada 3-0 and into the last eight at the World Cup for the second consecutive tournament.

rfi.title: Germany's anti-immigration AfD elects new leaders amid mass protests
rfi.description: Tens of thousands of demonstrators gathered in the eastern German city of Erfurt on Saturday, blocking major roads and disrupting public transport, but failed to stop the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from opening its annual party congress.

rfi.title: The 'other kick-off': NGOs warn of domestic violence spike during World Cup
rfi.description: With the World Cup in full swing, several NGOs have launched awareness campaigns to prevent domestic abuse – incidents of which studies have shown increase on match nights.

lemonde.description: L’étape du Tour de France d’aujourd’hui se tiendra sans public côté français. Le ministre de l’intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, est attendu dans les Pyrénées-Orientales cet après-midi. Des incendies touchent également le Gard, la Drôme, l’Aude et l’Ariège.

lemonde.title: Cédric Jubillar a reconnu dans une lettre avoir tué sa femme, Delphine Aussaguel, selon son avocat
lemonde.description: M. Jubillar, condamné à trente ans de réclusion criminelle en octobre 2025, s’était, jusqu’ici, toujours dit innocent. Le corps de Delphine n’a pas été retrouvé.

lemonde.title: Iran : aux funérailles de l’ancien Guide suprême Ali Khamenei, l’absence remarquée de Mojtaba, son fils et successeur
lemonde.description: Après les prières publiques, dimanche, le cortège funéraire doit traverser Téhéran, lundi, avant de rejoindre Qom pour un hommage du clergé chiite, mardi. La dépouille passera ensuite par les villes saintes irakiennes de Nadjaf et Kerbala, avant d’être inhumée, jeudi, à Machhad, ville d’origine du défunt.

lemonde.title: En Allemagne, le parti d’extrême droite AfD est traversé par de profondes divergences malgré l’unité affichée lors de son congrès
lemonde.description: Réunie en congrès à Erfurt, en Thuringe, les 4 et 5 juillet, la principale force d’opposition allemande se mobilise avant les scrutins régionaux du 6 septembre. Mais en son sein, des désaccords stratégiques entre l’Est et l’Ouest subsistent, qu’incarne le duo formé par Tino Chrupalla et Alice Weidel à la tête du parti.

lemonde.title: Un « démantèlement » d’ampleur des lois environnementales est en cours en Europe, alerte un collectif d’ONG
lemonde.description: Vingt mesures de dérégulation ou d’affaiblissement du droit de l’environnement ont été adoptées depuis 2024 au niveau de l’Union européenne ; trente nouveaux reculs sont en cours de discussion, ont comptabilisé les organisations non gouvernementales.

lemonde.title: « J’y croyais vraiment cette année ! » : à Rio, la déception des supporteurs du Brésil après l’élimination de la Coupe du monde 2026
lemonde.description: La Seleçao a été battue par la Norvège, dimanche, en huitièmes de finale du Mondial de football. Neymar a annoncé sa retraite internationale. Les supporteurs disent ne pas le regretter.

lemonde.title: Canicule : la motion de censure des Ecologistes ne sera pas votée par le PS, une motion « de posture politique », selon Maud Bregeon
lemonde.description: La motion de censure doit être débattue ce lundi après-midi à l’Assemblée nationale. « Face à la situation qu’on traverse, prétendre que censurer le gouvernement pourrait (…) apporter des réponses est un mensonge politique », selon la porte-parole du gouvernement, Maud Bregeon.

lemonde.title: Espace « no kids » : un rapport alerte sur l’invisibilisation des enfants dans l’espace public
lemonde.description: Ces dernières années, l’apparition dans des pays européens d’espaces interdits aux enfants dans des secteurs tels que l’hôtellerie, la restauration et les transports, a suscité des polémiques.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky appelle ses alliés à prendre des « décisions fermes » au sommet de l’OTAN
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien a condamné l’« attaque massive » lancée par la Russie dans la nuit, qui a fait au moins 11 morts à Kiev et 3 autres dans l’oblast de la capitale.

lemonde.title: Gaz : malgré la trêve au Moyen-Orient, l’Europe tarde à remplir ses stocks
lemonde.description: Les prix du gaz ont diminué bien moins rapidement que ceux du pétrole depuis le début des pourparlers qui ont eu lieu, à la mi-juin, entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran. Le signe d’un marché qui demeure plus tendu.

lemonde.description: Candidate potentielle pour la présidentielle de 2028, Sara Duterte risque une inéligibilité à vie. Elle est accusée de malversations, de corruption et de menaces de mort contre le président Ferdinand Marcos Jr, son colistier lors de l’élection de 2022.

france24fr.description: Le site spécialisé The Athletic annonce lundi que la Fédération royale belge de football a fait appel de la décision de la Fifa de lever la suspension de l’attaquant américain Folarin Balogun. L’instance avait annoncé la veille que le joueur des États-Unis pourrait jouer en 8e de finale du Mondial contre la Belgique, grâce à une modification de la sanction qui lui avait été infligée. Un allègement de peine qui aurait été directement demandé par le président Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Grèce : incendies près de Thessalonique, des habitants évacués
france24fr.description: Les pompiers grecs luttent toujours dimanche contre les flammes autour de deux usines près de la grande ville de Thessalonique, après un feu de forêt qui a entretemps pu être maîtrisé, selon eux.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : la Fifa blanchit Balogun après un coup de fil de Trump
france24fr.description: Le Mondial-2026 tient son scandale: contrarié par la suspension de l'Américain Folarin Balogun pour le huitième de finale lundi contre la Belgique, Donald Trump a appelé le président de la Fifa Gianni Infantino, et le joueur a finalement été autorisé à jouer, une ingérence qui suscite un tollé.

france24fr.title: Le président Macron va se rendre en Syrie, annonce la présidence syrienne
france24fr.description: ⁠Le président ​français Emmanuel Macron va se ​rendre en Syrie pour discuter des moyens de renforcer les relations  bilatérales ‌entre les ⁠deux pays et d'autres sujets d'intérêt mutuel, ‌a annoncé dimanche l'organisation média de ⁠la présidence syrienne.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela : au moins 3 342 morts, des corps non identifiés enterrés
france24fr.description: Le double tremblement de terre qui a dévasté le nord du Venezuela le 24 juin a fait plus de 3.000 morts, selon un nouveau bilan dimanche des autorités qui ont commencé à faire enterrer des victimes non identifiées.

france24fr.title: Le feu se poursuit dans les Pyrénées-Orientales, 10 000 personnes évacuées
france24fr.description: Quelque 10 000 personnes ont ⁠dû être évacuées dans ​les Pyrénées-Orientales en raison des incendies qui se poursuivent dans le département et ont déjà détruit 4 600 ​hectares de forêt, a déclaré lundi le ministre de l'Intérieur.

france24fr.title: La Syrie annonce une visite de Macron : l'Elysée n'a pas encore confirmé
Mondial-2026 : la Seleçao éliminée par la Norvège avant les quarts de finale
france24fr.description: Marine Resse, notre correspondante à Rio de Janeiro, décrypte la situation.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : l'équipe du Cap-Vert célébrée après son parcours
france24fr.description: La belle ⁠aventure du ​Cap-Vert à sa première Coupe du monde s'est achevée vendredi contre l'Argentine, en seizièmes de finale, ​mais les Requins bleus ont quitté le tournoi la tête haute après avoir bousculé les champions du monde en titre.

france24fr.title: Des bombardements russes font au moins 10 morts dans la région de Kiev
france24fr.description: Des bombardements russes ont fait au moins 10 morts lundi dans la région de Kiev à la veille d'un sommet de l'Otan à Ankara.

france24fr.title: Scandola, joyau corse sous pression : la biodiversité face à l'afflux de touristes
france24fr.description: Scandola, réserve naturelle classée à l'UNESCO sur les côtes de l'île de beauté, attire un nombre croissant de visiteurs du monde entier, séduits par ses paysages spectaculaires et sa riche vie marine. Mais protéger sa faune unique et son fragile écosystème marin devient un exercice d'équilibre de plus en plus délicat. Reportage de nos confrères de France 2, Audrey Richier et Virgile Liado.

france24fr.title: Canicule : l'Europe découvre sa dépendance asiatique pour les climatiseurs
france24fr.description: Les deux vagues de canicule de ce début d'été ont provoqué une ruée sur les climatiseurs en France et en Europe. Une demande qui met en lumière une dépendance industrielle massive envers l'Asie, en particulier la Chine, au moment où la climatisation devient progressivement un enjeu de santé publique.

france24fr.title: La Chine dit avoir effectué un tir d'essai de missile dans le Pacifique et suscite l'inquiétude
france24fr.description: La marine chinoise a procédé, lundi, à un tir d'essai d'un missile balistique à longue portée depuis l'un de ses sous-marins à propulsion nucléaire dans le Pacifique Sud. Une initiative rare qui a suscité des protestations et des inquiétudes de la part des pays de la région, comme le Japon et la Nouvelle-Zélande.

france24fr.title: La présidence syrienne annonce une visite d'Emmanuel Macron à Damas
france24fr.description: ⁠Le président ​français Emmanuel Macron va se ​rendre en Syrie pour y rencontrer le président intérimaire Ahmed al-Charaa, ‌a annoncé dimanche le service de presse de ⁠la présidence syrienne. La date du ​déplacement n'a pas été ​précisée.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : de Mussolini à Trump, quand la politique se mêle du football
france24fr.description: La Fifa a annulé la suspension du joueur américain Folarin Balogun ce dimanche, quelques jours avant le 8e de finale contre la Belgique. Une décision annoncée à la suite d'un appel personnel de Donald Trump. Ce n'est pas la première fois que la politique s'invite sur les terrains de la Coupe du monde.

france24fr.title: Féminicide : Cédric Jubillar finit par confesser le meurtre de son épouse Delphine
france24fr.description: Cédric Jubillar avait jusqu'ici nié toute implication dans la mort de son épouse Delphine, disparue dans la nuit du 15 au 16 décembre 2020 et dont le corps n'a jamais été retrouvé. L'homme est passé aux aveux, lundi, sept ans après le féminicide pour lequel il purge déjà 30 ans de prison. Il se dit prêt à donner des indications sur l'endroit où il a dissimulé le corps, selon son avocat.

france24fr.title: L'incendie des Pyrénées-Orientales toujours pas maîtrisé, les pompiers reprennent les opérations
france24fr.description: Le feu continue de brûler près de Perpignan, où les pompiers s'acharnent pour tenter de le maîtriser. Près de 10 000 habitants ont été évacués face à la progression des flammes, qui ont déjà détruit 4 600 hectares. Cinq personnes, dont deux pompiers, ont été blessées. L'arrivée de la 3e étape du Tour de France aux Angles est maintenue lundi, mais se déroulera sans public côté français.

zeit.description: Wegen massiver Absatzrückgänge will der Sportwagenhersteller weitere Stellen abbauen. Der Fokus liege im Management. Ende Juli soll ein Zukunftspaket vorgestellt werden.

spiegel.title: Prinz Harry reist nach London – jetzt gibt es Streit über seinen Schlafplatz
spiegel.description: Prinz Harry fliegt nach England und lässt verkünden, dass er im Buckingham Palace nächtigen wird. Doch der Palast widerspricht.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Uefa wirft Fifa im Fall Balogun vor, »rote Linie« überschritten zu haben
spiegel.description: »Nicht zu rechtfertigen«: Der europäische Fußballverband reagiert mit harscher Kritik auf die Aufhebung der Sperre für Folarin Balogun durch die Fifa. Zuvor soll sich Donald Trump für den US-Stürmer eingesetzt haben. Alles Wichtige zu WM-Tag 26.

spiegel.title: Easyjet gibt Widerstand gegen Übernahme von US-Investor Castlelake auf
spiegel.description: Nach wochenlangem Ringen stimmt der britische Billigflieger Easyjet einer Übernahme durch den US-Investor Castlelake zu. Doch damit ist das Pokerspiel noch keineswegs beendet.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Wie ich als Student Zeuge eines Flugzeugunglücks wurde
spiegel.description: SPIEGEL-Leser Peter Hamel jobbte als Student am Hamburger Flughafen. An einem ruhigen Nachmittag hörte er plötzlich ein lautes Krachen, gefolgt von Stille. Und rannte aufs Rollfeld.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Wie die NSDAP so stark werden konnte – Podcast
spiegel.description: Nicht nur in Deutschland, auch in Österreich war die NSDAP eine Massenbewegung. Und zwar lange, bevor Adolf Hitler den »Anschluss« seiner Heimat ans Deutsche Reich erklärte.

spiegel.title: Robert Habeck berät künftig eine dänische Investmentgesellschaft
spiegel.description: Ex-Wirtschaftsminister Robert Habeck vertieft seine beruflichen Verbindungen nach Dänemark. Ab August steigt der Grüne bei einem Immobilieninvestor ein. Auch bei seiner Forschungsarbeit gibt es einen Wechsel.

spiegel.title: England besiegt Mexiko bei WM: Den Tank bis auf den allerletzten Tropfen leergefahren
spiegel.description: Fast 80.000 Zuschauer gegen sich, lange in Unterzahl, dazu die dünne Luft auf 2200 Metern: England steht nach einem denkwürdigen Abend im Viertelfinale. Doch Angreifer Harry Kane deutet an, was nun droht: der Kampf gegen die Erschöpfung.

spiegel.title: Reaktionen aus Oslo auf WM-Sieg gegen Brasilien: »Es ist völlig surreal«
spiegel.description: Der Ruder-Schlachtruf hat wieder Wirkung gezeigt: Mit dem 2:1 gegen Brasilien im WM-Achtelfinale hat Norwegen Fußballgeschichte geschrieben. Die Fans können ihr Glück kaum fassen. Reaktionen im Video.

spiegel.title: »Rente mit 63«: SPD-Sozialexperte fordert Zehn-Jahres-Frist für Abschaffung
spiegel.description: Wegen der Rente hatten sich Union und SPD wochenlang in der Wolle. Nun wollen verschiedene Politiker einen Teil des Reformpakets um Jahre nach hinten verschieben – und verweisen auf das Bundesverfassungsgericht.

spiegel.title: Bruce Springsteen verteidigt kritischen Patriotismus
spiegel.description: Bruce Springsteen zählt zu den erbittertsten Kritikern von US-Präsident Donald Trump. Macht ihn das zu einem schlechten Patrioten? Der 76-Jährige hat darauf eine klare Antwort.

spiegel.title: Kapitalrente: Wie Anja Mikus Milliarden für die Altersvorsorge anlegen soll
spiegel.description: Finanzmanagerin Anja Mikus leitet den Atomfonds Kenfo. Der investiert Milliarden an Aktienmärkten – bald vielleicht auch für die neue Kapitalrente.

spiegel.title: Baden-Württemberg: Schüsse in Offenburg – zwei Tote
spiegel.description: Am Montagmorgen sind in Offenburg ein Mann und eine Frau erschossen worden. Es läuft ein größerer Polizeieinsatz.

spiegel.title: Hitzewelle in Südfrankreich: Waldbrandgefahr bremst die Tour de France aus
spiegel.description: In Südfrankreich müssen Tausende Anwohner wegen der Waldbrände ihre Häuser verlassen. Die dritte Etappe der Tour de France soll ohne Zuschauer stattfinden.

spiegel.title: 250 Years: American Democracy Has Survived 250 Years, But Can It Survive Trump?
spiegel.description: Democracy is a tenacious beast, but it has been riven by contradictions ever since the Declaration of Independence. Nowhere are those contradictions in such sharp relief as in Trump's America.

spiegel.title: Australien: Regierung kritisiert chinesischen Raketentest als destabilisierend
spiegel.description: Erstmals seit zwei Jahren hat Chinas Volksbefreiungsarmee im Pazifik eine Interkontinentalrakete ins Meer gefeuert – offenbar mit einem Übungssprengkopf. Australien hält das Manöver für »destabilisierend«.

spiegel.title: WM-Aus für Brasilien gegen Norwegen: Eine Ära endet. Und das ist gut so
spiegel.description: So früh wie seit 36 Jahren nicht mehr ist Brasilien bei der WM gescheitert. Neymar weinte bittere Tränen und trat zurück. Das ist eine gute Nachricht für die Seleção.

spiegel.title: Bertelsmann-Studie: Unternehmen befürchten Schwächung der Demokratie
spiegel.description: Die zunehmend unversöhnliche Auseinandersetzung über politische Fragen belastet inzwischen auch das Klima in den Betrieben. Manager und Managerinnen sehen darin eine Gefahr für die Demokratie.

spiegel.title: New York City: Wasserflugzeug kentert im East River
spiegel.description: Ein Wasserflugzeug mit acht Passagieren an Bord ist mitten in New York unkontrolliert gelandet und zum Teil gekentert. Es gab zwei Leichtverletzte, die Bundesluftfahrtbehörde ermittelt.

phys-org.title: Researchers use AI to evaluate a systematic framework to describe molecular order in liquid water
phys-org.description: Water is the most abundant liquid on Earth's surface, and it is highly anomalous compared with other liquids because it expands upon freezing. The anomalies in water have been linked to how its microscopic structure changes with temperature and pressure. However, there is no systematic scheme for characterizing these structural changes.

phys-org.title: How we can coexist with coyotes, and other lessons from Stanley Park: Q&A with zoologists
phys-org.description: Researchers are sharing lessons from the unprecedented Stanley Park coyote attacks from 2020 to 2021 to help people better coexist with urban wildlife.

phys-org.title: Neutral lipids enable precision control over supramolecular polymerization
phys-org.description: The formation of supramolecular polymers within living cells is an emerging strategy for regulating cellular functions, and lipid droplets (LDs) are promising environments for such processes. LDs are cellular organelles composed mainly of neutral lipids, such as triacylglycerols and cholesterol esters, and are deeply involved in cellular functions. However, the self-assembly of supramolecular polymers in neutral lipid-rich environments such as LDs is not well understood.

phys-org.title: 'Major' damage as super typhoon hits US islands
phys-org.description: A "super typhoon" with the force of a Category 5 hurricane tore through the U.S. Pacific territories of the Northern Marianas and Guam on Monday, with authorities saying they had received reports of "major" damage on the small island of Rota.

phys-org.title: China's space probe reaches asteroid after 1-billion-kilometer chase for first sample return
phys-org.description: China's Tianwen-2 space probe, which is set to bring back samples from an asteroid for research, has reached its target after traveling 1 billion kilometers (620 million miles) over more than a year, the Chinese space agency said Monday.

phys-org.title: Thousands flee raging wildfires in southern Europe
phys-org.description: Wildfires raged across Southern Europe on Monday, forcing thousands of people to evacuate their homes and prompting officials to ban spectators from a stage of the storied Tour de France cycling race.

phys-org.title: Euclid discovers the most ancient quasars in the universe
phys-org.description: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 of the most ancient quasars ever found. Two of these giant and dazzling galaxy cores, powered by gargantuan black holes, are the earliest quasars yet observed in cosmic history. They shone with the light of a trillion suns when the universe was 670 million years old—just 5% of its current age.

phys-org.title: The world's oceans are the hottest on record for June—and El Niño is set to turn up the heat even more
phys-org.description: The world's oceans are the hottest on record for June, pushing past records set during the 2023–24 El Niño years.

phys-org.title: An island of calm at the violent heart of the galaxy
phys-org.description: Where would you go to watch a star being born? Probably not the heart of the Milky Way, which is about the most violent neighborhood our galaxy has to offer, a maelstrom of gas churning so fast and so chaotically that you would think nothing could ever settle there long enough to collapse into a star. And yet stars do form in that turmoil, and astronomers have just begun to work out how by finding an unexpected pocket of calm in the chaos.

phys-org.title: Rats show empathy, according to model
phys-org.description: A rat first frees a cagemate rat and then shares food with it. Is this animal just as empathetic as humans? In an American study from 2011, researchers observed that rats first freed their fellow rats from a cage and then shared food with them instead of leaving them in the cage and eating alone; this means they showed empathy. But do they have the same capacity for empathy as we humans, or do we differ in that regard?

phys-org.title: Spring songbirds may help pollinate UK trees, with pollen on 89% of studied birds
phys-org.description: The warblers—those harbingers of spring in the U.K.—have an unappreciated talent of a different sort. Common U.K. birds, including chiffchaffs and blackcaps, are playing a real role in the pollination of plants, according to new research in the Journal of Ecology.

phys-org.title: Deuterium in comets tells interesting tales
phys-org.description: Comets have played an interesting role in the history of astronomy. Since antiquity, many cultures saw them as omens or spirits, portending good or bad news for kings, queens and emperors. Over the past few hundred years, however, astronomers have studied them intently to understand the science behind these visitors to the inner solar system. Today, we know that these ghostly apparitions in the sky are dirty balls of ice and rock blasting through space, scattering dust and gases as they go.

phys-org.title: European cities short on shade as heat waves hit, urban mapping reveals
phys-org.description: More than four in five homes and workplaces across 25 European cities have less nearby tree canopy than what is needed for meaningful cooling, according to an open-data analysis by an urban greening expert.

phys-org.title: Mars express captures dozens of dust devils in Mars valley
phys-org.description: Dust devils are a regular feature on Mars. Just like those found on Earth, these mini whirlwinds form when parts of Mars are warmed by the sun, causing air above the surface to swirl upward and carry dust with it. But in Mars' lower gravity (38% that of Earth), these devils grow much larger, reaching up to 8 km (5 miles) in height and speeds of up to 45 meters per second (150 feet per second). Although it is only 1.8 billion light-years away from us, the central black hole in the galaxy exhibits properties typical of the early universe. phys-org.title: Laughter may date back 15 million years, shared by humans and great apes

phys-org.title: Japan space probe skims asteroid in test for planetary defense
phys-org.description: A Japanese space probe performed a flyby of a near-Earth asteroid on Sunday in a test mission for technology that could help protect the planet from space rocks.

phys-org.title: Scattered bronze bells in Chinese lord's 2,600-year-old tomb point to ritual deactivation

But the most mysterious part of all: This was apparently no accident, with the family of the tomb's owner having chosen to "deactivate" the bells when their powers were no longer needed.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing

Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.

proj-syn.title: The Putin Escalation Risk
proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. The temptation to escape his predicament through a game-changing attack will grow stronger.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s New German Question
proj-syn.description: Without a EU-level framework capable of turning resources into scale, the bloc’s defense capabilities will remain limited, no matter how much member countries spends. If Germany, in particular, insists on going it alone, Europe could remain fully dependent on the US for key assets.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
proj-syn.description: While Nobel laureate economists Paul Krugman and Philippe Aghion disagree over how to measure Europe’s productivity gap with the United States, both overlook the value of its accumulated assets. That blind spot obscures the real story: Europe is living off a remarkable inheritance it has yet to convert into new growth.

proj-syn.title: NATO Needs a Defense Market
proj-syn.description: To convert NATO members' resources into military capabilities, setting defense as a strategic priority, increasing spending, and improving procurement systems are all steps in the right direction. But member countries will need to expand their industrial capacity—and that requires much more.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Choices Shaping our Children’s Health
proj-syn.description: Around the world, childhood is being reprogrammed by digital technologies that shape how young people learn, play, and connect. But children and young people are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity, which is why we must shape digital environments that protect and support their healthy development.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy’s Ancient Origins
proj-syn.description: The struggle between democracy and oligarchy in classical Greece was bitter, with oligarchies relying on skillfully designed political institutions to shore up unpopular regimes. As concerns grow over the “rule of the few” in the United States, Americans should consider how their own institutions are doing oligarchs’ work for them.

proj-syn.title: How Modi Has Remade India
proj-syn.description: Over the last 12 years, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has overseen dizzying progress in economic modernization and state capacity-building, as well as dismaying setbacks on institutional independence and minority inclusion. This record offers important insights into how India will navigate the 21st century.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI, Energy And Biotech Lead The Way
crunchbase.description: U.S. startups announced sizable funding rounds at a steady clip during a truncated holiday week, with energy and AI leading the way. Houston-based energy startup Joulent secured the biggest round, a $1.75 billion strategic financing.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Global Startup Investment Hit Record $510B In H1 2026 As AI Boom Accelerates Funding And Exits
crunchbase.description: Investors poured more than $200 billion into startups globally in the just-ended quarter, making Q2 2026 the second-largest quarter on record, our data shows. And, with IPOs and acquisitions returning in force, the second quarter notched one of the strongest periods for venture-backed exits in years.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker

crunchbase.title: London-Based Tapestry VC Closes On $80M Third Fund To Invest In Repeat European Founders
crunchbase.description: Tapestry VC has closed an $80 million third fund to double down on Europe’s repeat founders and expects the coming wave of AI exits to produce yet another generation of experienced founders.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: No More Side Hustles: Why AI Startup Omnea Will Give Employees $250K To Openly Plan Their Next Startup
crunchbase.description: Omnea, a London-based artificial intelligence software company that helps businesses manage their supplier spending, is challenging traditional venture models with the launch of the Omnea Future Founders Fund to give its employees who have completed five years of service a chance to pitch for $250,000 in seed funding to launch their own companies.

crunchbase.title: We Need To Save Venture Capital From Bad Data
crunchbase.description: Venture capital firms are using AI the wrong way, argues Gilion's Henrik Landgren, who says that building better data infrastructure and connecting directly to sources like financial, payment and accounting systems would improve due diligence, help investors identify overlooked startups, and make investment decisions both faster and more accurate.

crunchbase.title: GV’s Dave Munichiello On Qualcomm’s Modular Purchase, The Firm’s 10x Return And The Shift In AI Software
crunchbase.description: The artificial intelligence space saw two major developments last week that highlight how technology companies are trying to manage the soaring costs and complexity of AI computing. In an interview with Crunchbase News, Dave Munichiello, a managing partner at GV, discusses the mechanics behind the Qualcomm-Modular deal, the practical realities of managing hardware scarcity, and what the current wave of consolidation means for the future of independent startups.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Q2 Brought The Most Billion-Dollar Startup Exits Since 2021
crunchbase.description: Startup exits valued at $1 billion or more are now more numerous than at any point since the 2021 market peak, Crunchbase data shows. The trend we’re seeing for the second quarter of 2026 includes both the largest venture-backed exit of all time and a bevy of other comparatively tinier but still sizable startup exits through acquisition or IPO.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives Another Spree Of Megadeals
crunchbase.description: This week, most of the largest U.S. startup funding rounds centered around the sector one would suspect: artificial intelligence. Beyond that, the next-biggest area for startup funding was biotech.

crunchbase.title: 6 Startup Investors On What It Will Take To Fund More Black Founders
crunchbase.description: In the final installment of our series on the state of venture investment to Black-founded startups, six investors offer their advice for overlooked founders and explain how the venture industry can broaden access to capital by rethinking sourcing, networks and long-held investing patterns.
